deckTitle: Pattern B — Sovereign Silos: One Project, One Perimeter, One Key per Tenant
deckSubtitle: Reusing the 80% 5-Hop Cymbal core inside dedicated VPC-SC / PAB / CMEK tenant projects with air-gapped Gemma 3 on GKE
tldr: Regulated tenants (OCC/FDIC, DORA, HIPAA, public sector) often prohibit shared compute, shared databases, and platform-owned keys.
Pattern B keeps core-cymbal-agent unchanged and adds a 20% delta: mTLS SPIFFE pinning, IAM PAB, VPC-SC perimeter, CMEK kill-switch, Gemma 3 on GKE.
Each tenant gets a dedicated project: cymbal-finvault-silo-prod and cymbal-retailstream-silo-prod, each with its own agent-memory-cmek key.
Revoking the tenant CMEK halts every agent turn at Hop 3 with HTTP 423 KMS_KEY_DISABLED; all 6 sovereign security tests pass.
Trade-off: zero noisy neighbours and simple per-project quotas versus a higher per-tenant infrastructure floor and multi-project operations.

sections.heading: Why Pooled Isolation Is Not Enough
bullets: Auditors ask whether any other customer could ever touch your compute, storage, or key — not just whether data is logically separated.
Four drivers: zero physical blast radius, customer-revocable encryption key, hard identity boundary, no multi-tenant model endpoints.
FinVault Bank (Google OIDC, Workspace + Jira) and RetailStream Corp (Entra ID, SharePoint + ServiceNow) each receive a sovereign silo.
Pattern A remains the right answer for Standard SaaS tiers thanks to ContextCacheConfig prefix caching (up to 90% COGS savings).

sections.heading: The Sovereign Silo Model
bullets: PatternBSiloedService wraps CymbalMultiTenantRuntime and checks mTLS SPIFFE, PAB, and VPC-SC egress before the 5-Hop pipeline runs.
VPC-SC restricts aiplatform, discoveryengine, modelarmor, alloydb, storage, and bigquery APIs so valid credentials cannot exfiltrate.
Dedicated CMEK AlloyDB, 5-Level Memory Bank, BigQuery audit, GKE disks, and runtime all depend on one tenant key: agent-memory-cmek.
FinVault runs air-gapped gemma-3-27b-it-vllm on private GKE; RetailStream runs Gemini 2.5 Pro with dedicated Provisioned Throughput.

sections.heading: 5-Hop Chain Inside a Silo
bullets: Hop 1 strips forged X-Tenant-ID headers, verifies IdP JWT, performs RFC 8693 OBO + DPoP, and mints PATTERN_B_SILOED context.
Hop 2 registry PDP and before_agent_callback pruning become defence-in-depth behind PAB and VPC-SC.
Hop 3 resolves silo_cmek_key_uri; a disabled key returns DENY 423 KMS_KEY_DISABLED before any Memory Bank or model call.
Hop 4 Model Armor and Hop 5 AlloyDB RLS + BigQuery OTel run unchanged, inside dedicated CMEK-encrypted resources.

sections.heading: Verification: 6 Sovereign Security Tests
bullets: TEST 1: spoofed SPIFFE cert at FinVault ingress → 401 MTLS_CERTIFICATE_MISMATCH.
TEST 2: FinVault principal targets RetailStream project → 403 PAB_BOUNDARY_VIOLATION.
TEST 3: export to external-attacker-exfil-proj → 403 VPC_SERVICE_CONTROLS_PERMISSION_DENIED.
TEST 4A/4B/5: CMEK revoke → 423; restore → 200 with AirGapped-GKE-Gemma3-27B response prefix.
TEST 6: RetailStream silo CMEK revoke/restore parity verified; suite reports 100% VERIFIED.

sections.heading: Provisioning, Sign-Off & Blueprint
bullets: 3.2 runbook: create projects, enable 7 APIs, create finvault-kr/agent-memory-cmek (90-day rotation), bind finvault-sovereign-pab at org level.
3.4 sign-off: VPC-SC, PAB, CMEK kill-switch, and mTLS + air-gapped Gemma 3 all SIGNED OFF by GCP Security and GEAP Product Engineering.
3.6 Terraform blueprint provisions CMEK key, perimeter_<tenant>_sovereign, sovereign VPC, and <tenant>-airgapped-gemma3-gke per apply.
3.8 codelab (90 min, 5 modules) and 3.9 go/demos video script reuse the same verification gates.

sections.heading: Trade-Offs & What Comes Next
bullets: Pattern B is a different economic contract: dedicated quotas and zero noisy neighbours at a higher per-tenant floor.
The GKE GPU floor dominates cost when air-gapped inference is mandated — offer it as an explicit option, not a default.
Rehearse CMEK restoration with each customer SOC; revocation is immediate and total.
Workstream 4 (Pattern C) blends pooled and sovereign tiers via Private Service Connect spokes and zero-downtime tier migration.

diagrams.title: Pattern B: Zero-Trust Sovereign Silos (VPC-SC, IAM PAB, CMEK & Air-Gapped Gemma 3 on GKE)
talkingPoints: Follow badges 1→7: mTLS Request enters from the SPIFFE clients; Silo Response or HTTP 423 Locked returns on the same trunk.
Routing hub: Cloud Armor SPIFFE pinning, Model Armor edge filter, IAM PAB Verifier, External ALB, Sovereign Hub Router.
Governance hub: Security Command Center, Cloud KMS / EKM Key, and the Silo Security Suite 6/6 Sovereign Tests PASS card.
Dashed line 'CMEK state & VPC-SC audit monitoring' feeds both silos — the signal Hop 3 uses to refuse work instantly.
Left spoke: Perimeter Alpha / cymbal-finvault-silo-prod with Gemma 3 (27B) GKE air-gapped inference and Private GKE Zero Egress.
Right spoke: Perimeter Beta / cymbal-retailstream-silo-prod with Gemini 2.5 Pro PT and Local Silo MCP Entra SharePoint & SNOW.

diagrams.title: Pattern B Provisioning Topology: Org → Per-Tenant Silo Projects, VPC-SC Perimeters, IAM PAB & Cloud KMS CMEK Keys
talkingPoints: One org, two dedicated tenant projects — cymbal-finvault-silo-prod and cymbal-retailstream-silo-prod — created under ORG_ID and linked to one billing account.
Bootstrap enables seven silo APIs per project: aiplatform, discoveryengine, modelarmor, container, cloudkms, alloydb and accesscontextmanager.
Per-tenant Cloud KMS: key ring finvault-kr in us-central1 with crypto key agent-memory-cmek, purpose encryption, 90-day (7776000s) rotation.
The Vertex AI service agent (service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-aiplatform) receives roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the tenant key only.
Org-level IAM Principal Access Boundary finvault-sovereign-pab restricts FinVault principals strictly to the FinVault silo project resource.
Step 7 closes the loop: run_silo_security_tests.py replays perimeter exfiltration and CMEK revocation checks before the silo is declared live.

diagrams.title: Terraform Blueprint Resource Graph: Provider → Cloud KMS CMEK → VPC-SC Perimeter → Sovereign VPC → Private Air-Gapped GKE (Gemma 3)
talkingPoints: A single root module (Terraform >= 1.5.0, hashicorp/google >= 5.30.0) provisions one sovereign silo per tenant from five variables in terraform.tfvars.
google_kms_key_ring.tenant_silo_keyring (${tenant_id}-sovereign-kr) and google_kms_crypto_key.tenant_agent_cmek (agent-memory-cmek, 90-day rotation) come first.
google_access_context_manager_service_perimeter.tenant_sovereign_perimeter binds projects/${tenant_silo_project_number} and restricts eight APIs.
Restricted services: aiplatform, discoveryengine, modelarmor, alloydb, bigquery, storage, cloudkms and container — no path out of the perimeter.
google_compute_network.tenant_silo_vpc and tenant_silo_subnet (10.40.0.0/20, Private Google Access) host the private GKE Autopilot cluster.
google_container_cluster.airgapped_gemma3_cluster uses private nodes/endpoint and database_encryption.key_name = the CMEK key, surfaced via two outputs.

takeaways: Choose Pattern B only when a contract demands a dedicated blast radius, a customer-revocable key, or no multi-tenant model endpoints.
Keep the governance code identical across patterns; pay for infrastructure, not for a second engineering team.
PAB answers 'which projects may this principal ever reach?' — it blocks lateral movement even when another project's IAM is wrong.
Make the tenant CMEK the single dependency for runtime, memory, data, and audit so one key disable is a complete kill-switch.
Prove every control with the 6-test suite before onboarding, and keep the results visible on the architecture diagram.
callToAction: Run run_silo_security_tests.py, apply the 3.6 Terraform silo blueprint for one tenant, and book the 90-minute Pattern B codelab with your security team.
